finding.summary: Canonical backend design doc not updated for the new OAuth state cookie / pre-user state validation

verdict.reason: The finding claims no canonical design doc absorbed the new OAuth state cookie / pre-user state validation. A counterexample exists: docs/design/rest-api.md — which docs/design/README.md:159 designates as the canonical doc for "CLI auth endpoints" — was updated with exactly this content. rest-api.md:334-345 documents that non-CLI (web) requests now get a state "mirrored into the `wafflebase_oauth_state` cookie, checked on the callback"; rest-api.md:346-350 documents that the callback "validates `state` before it touches a user, so a callback it did not start creates no account … must match the browser's `wafflebase_oauth_state` cookie (a missing state is refused)" — i.e. the exact pre-`findOrCreateUser` validation; rest-api.md:383 adds a Risks row for the web-flow CSRF mitigation (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, constant-time, single-use, cookie-vs-map rationale), matching packages/backend/src/auth/cookies.ts:16-35 and github-auth.guard.ts:58-83. This is an update to a pre-existing canonical section ("### 7. CLI Auth Endpoints") that already held the CLI OAuth-state mechanics, not a parallel file, satisfying CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 and 57-61. backend.md:103-115 is a summary-level API reference that already omitted the pre-existing GitHubAuthGuard/CLI state machinery (it still says "AuthGuard('github')" while the guard has been GitHubAuthGuard since the earlier CLI-login work), and its listed callback steps remain true and correctly ordered; re-syncing that summary is doc polish (minor), not a missing-design-doc violation.

finding.summary: Web-flow OAuth CSRF binding is unrequested scope for the #586 CLI exit-code task, in files a sibling PR is documented to own
finding.evidence: `docs/tasks/active/20260803-cli-system-exit-code-todo.md` scopes this work to the CLI exit-code contract (Approach items 1-7: `errors.ts`, `outputError`, `HttpClient`, command throw sites, import flows, `login`, docs). The diff additionally rewrites the backend's web OAuth flow (new `cookies.ts`, cookie-mirrored `state` in the guard, `consumeWebOAuthState` in the controller), a backend auth architecture change unrelated to CLI exit codes. The branch's own lessons file (`docs/tasks/active/20260803-cli-system-exit-code-lessons.md:220-233`) records that PR #786 already ships browser-binding work "in the same three files this branch touches" (`github-auth.guard.ts`, `auth.controller.ts`) and that writing a second version there "would have guaranteed a conflict" — the same argument applies to this web-flow binding. Worth confirming this belongs on this branch rather than #786.

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists as described. `packages/backend/src/auth/cookies.ts:16-35` is a new module for a web OAuth state cookie; `github-auth.guard.ts:67-83` mints a random 32-byte `state`, mirrors it into `OAUTH_STATE_COOKIE_NAME`, and passes it via `req.__oauthState`; `auth.controller.ts:25,127,250-256` adds `consumeWebOAuthState()` to validate/clear it. This is a backend web-OAuth architecture change. The originating task doc `docs/tasks/active/20260803-cli-system-exit-code-todo.md:18-51` scopes the work to the CLI exit-code contract (errors.ts, outputError, HttpClient, throw sites, import flows, login, docs), and its checklist (lines 54-77) — which does list other security controls added mid-branch (CLI nonce binding, image SSRF gate, DNS pin, proxies) — contains no web-flow OAuth state item, so the web-flow binding is unrequested relative to #586. The branch's own lessons file (lines 220-233) records that PR #786 already ships browser-binding OAuth work in `github-auth.guard.ts` and `auth.controller.ts`, the same two files this change edits, and that a second version there would guarantee a conflict; that passage is about the `?mode=cli` entry specifically, so the reviewer's extension to the web flow is an inference, but the file-level overlap is literal. Mitigating: the change is folded into the canonical design doc rather than a parallel one (`docs/design/rest-api.md:334-349`, risk table 382-383), and lessons.md:58-60 records a repo stance favoring shipping adjacent controls with the code they protect. Those weaken the severity but do not make the code absent, unreachable, or outside this lens — scope creep is explicitly in the design-fit lane. No named refutation ground applies, so the finding stands; confidence is low because whether this rises to blocking is a judgement call, not a factual gap.
